gaps.text: Whether the statement file says what the paper claims was judged by AI readers only; no machine checks it.
Remark N.6 (the permanent is not approximated by determinants of polynomial size) is the one numbered statement with no Lean theorem.
The release's own check runs two kernels (Lean's and nanoda) on one machine.
The proof gives no value for the size m₀ from which the bound holds.
The authors did not analyse relativization or algebrization.
No human mathematician has checked the development, the statement file or the proofs.

rows.title: Pin the release: every file hashed at its commit
rows.note: 333 files, 324 Lean files, 72,932 lines; Lean v4.33.1, Mathlib 0df444a3.

rows.title: Pre-register the rows and the verdict rule, timestamped on Bitcoin, before any run
rows.note: Sealed and stamped 23:57 UTC on 23 Nov, before any run; first seal superseded within a minute (a date written ahead of the clock, deviation D0). Bitcoin confirms the stamp from block 977295 (00:19 UTC on 24 Nov), by which time rows PIN and K0 had finished: for those two the order rests on our own log (deviation D4).

rows.title: Build the release; list its axioms; search for unsafe code
rows.note: built in 554 s (9,032 modules), exit 0; the only sorry warnings are the five in Challenge.lean (lines 17–29), as the README says; no native_decide, implemented_by, extern or axiom declaration in the 324 Lean files; all five theorems depend only on propext, Classical.choice, Quot.sound.

rows.title: The release's own check (Comparator, Lean's kernel, nanoda), at its own pins
rows.note: the release's own script, unmodified, at its own pins (Comparator 57567492, nanoda 68d5ca9d, landrun 811cfff5 sandboxing): "Your solution is okay!", all 1 configuration accepted, 419 s.

rows.title: nanoda at a second version
rows.note: nanoda (ammkrn/nanoda_lib 0da9f98f, a second version) on our export of the five theorems' closure (60,921 declarations): "Checked 63,236 declarations with no typechecker errors" (its one "pretty printer error", "Unable to print axioms", is its acceptance form with axiom printing on and no destination set, as in our RH audit).

rows.title: con-leche, a third independently written checker
rows.note: con-leche 5ea446d5 accepted all 60,921 declarations of the export (--verified), and con-leche --compare justified each of the five theorems against Challenge.lean exported separately.

rows.title: Lean's own checker, replayed from scratch
rows.note: Lean's own checker replayed the five theorems' whole closure from scratch (leanchecker --fresh Solution): exit 0 after 35 min 39 s, 10.2 GB peak, no message.

rows.title: A second machine that never ran the release's code
rows.note: a second machine (EU-RO-1, 8 vCPU) that never ran the release's proofs: the official Lean v4.33.1 (GitHub's digest), the checkers built from source, a workspace with only Mathlib and the two statement files. The first machine's export arrived with its recorded sha256; nanoda accepted it, con-leche --compare justified the five theorems against the challenge exported there, and both controls were refused (C1 by con-leche; C2 by nanoda and con-leche). The challenge exported there is byte-identical to the first machine's. All 5 gates held, 01:08–01:10 UTC; the machine is deleted.

rows.title: Control: one symbol changed in a statement must be refused
rows.note: refused twice: Comparator, "Challenge and solution theorem statement do not match: Solution.permanent_over_real"; con-leche --compare, "the solution's Solution.permanent_over_real has another type".

rows.title: Control: a theorem re-typed as False must be refused
rows.note: refused twice: nanoda stopped on a failed definitional-equality check (exit 101); con-leche, "type mismatch in theorem Solution.mainTheorem".

rows.title: Census: what the five theorems actually use
rows.note: the five theorems reach 62,499 constants in 2,057 of the 11,334 modules imported; 320 of the release's 321 modules are used, the one unused being Paper.Ryser (the permanent's Ryser formula, not needed on the route). The first run of the census script failed on two Lean API names (deviation D2).

rows.title: The paper's Table 3 checked against the Lean names
rows.note: all 87 Lean names in the paper's Table 3 exist; 67 lie on the route of the five theorems; the four statements Appendix Q.3 says are off the route (Theorem L.2, Corollary L.3, Proposition E.5, Theorem E.6) are off it; the other 16 off the route are definitions and second names.

rows.title: Two blind statements, written from the textbooks without seeing the release's
rows.note: both blind statements written without seeing the release's and sealed before elaboration (B 00:03, A 00:12 UTC); both elaborated with no repair at all.

rows.title: Bridge: each blind statement proved from the release's theorems
rows.note: both blind statements, five propositions each, proved from the release's theorems (bridge A: a program of length ℓ becomes a release circuit of 4ℓ + 2 gates and the constant halves; bridge B: gate for gate, same constant). Replayed by the control room: Comparator, with OUR blind statement as the challenge, "Your solution is okay!" for both; nanoda (second version) checked 63,485 and 63,380 declarations with no error; con-leche --compare justified 5 of 5 for each. Lean's own checker replayed both bridges from scratch, exit 0 (36 min each).

rows.title: Anchors: the statement is not vacuous and means circuits, not formulas
rows.note: proved on the release's definitions and on both blind statements': every polynomial has a circuit (the bound is not vacuous); padding; reuse (X^(2^k) in k + 1 gates: circuits, not formulas); an exact circuit is an approximating one; the bound beats every polynomial; from the main theorem alone the permanent (characteristic ≠ 2) and Hamiltonian-cycle families are not in VP. Replayed: Comparator accepted all three sets (11, 11 and 7 theorems), nanoda and con-leche accepted them.

rows.title: Red controls: planted false versions proved false
rows.note: the planted claim "the main bound holds for the dense power (Σ x_ij)^m" is PROVED FALSE in Lean (a circuit of 2m² − 1 + k gates for m = 2^k), over ℚ, over every commutative semiring, in the main theorem's own shape, and for both blind statements. The characteristic-2 control waits for phase 3.

rows.title: An adversarial reading of every definition
rows.note: the reading found nothing material in 42 items; its 23 proposed Lean tests are proved (70 theorems, standard axioms only; one repair: an "open Classical in" the release's own definition also uses), replayed by the control room with nanoda and con-leche. The one unsure item (the exact wording of four books) is closed by bridge A.

rows.title: Fill gap G2: the determinant's small circuits, then Remark N.6, in Lean
rows.note: the statement is written in Lean (corpus/vp-vnp/lean/n6/N6Statement.lean: the determinant has small circuits; Remark N.6; the control in characteristic 2), elaborated at the release's pins and sealed at 02:38 UTC on 24 Nov, before any proof. Two provers that do not see each other (a Claude agent, GPT-6.2-astra) are working on the determinant's circuit; nothing is proved yet.

rows.title: What the theorem says in numbers: the constant, and the missing m₀
rows.note: read from the Lean and the paper, line by line (corpus/vp-vnp/NC.md): the proof's constant is c = 1/1600² (Paper/Fields.lean line 87, Paper/Approximate.lean line 295), so the bound exceeds m² only when log₂ m > (2·1600²)³ ≈ 1.3·10²⁰; m₀ is M₁ + M₂ + 2 with M₁, M₂ taken from existence statements, and the paper says the proof gives no value for it. A reading, not a machine check.

independence: The claim was made by a Claude model and Claude models are on this panel. Independence here is by procedure: statements written without seeing the release's, checkers written by other people (Lean's kernel, nanoda, con-leche), one blind statement by a non-Anthropic model, and every rule sealed before the run.
